Homework exercise · Week 1

Dragon Door

Python in Thonny Work in pairs

Goal: practice and, or and f-strings.

The dragon door opens if:

  • you have the golden key and you are level 3 or more, or
  • you are level 10 or more (legends do not need keys).
  1. Open starter.py in Thonny.
  2. TODO 1: change the if line in door_opens(). Brackets help: (has_key and level >= 3) or level >= 10.
  3. TODO 2: make the welcome message use an f-string with the hero name.
  4. Run it with these answers and check the door does the right thing: key yes + level 5 (opens), key yes + level 2 (shut), key no + level 12 (opens).

Extra: add a third way in: a secret password typed by the player. (Only a made-up game password, never a real one!)

Starter code

Open starter.py in Thonny, or copy the code below into a new file and save it as starter.py.

# Dragon Door
# The dragon door opens if you have the golden key AND you are level 3 or
# more, OR if you are level 10 or more (legends do not need keys).


def door_opens(has_key, level):
    """Return True if the dragon door opens, otherwise False."""
    # TODO 1: change this line. Use "and", "or" and brackets ( ).
    if has_key:
        return True
    else:
        return False


if __name__ == "__main__":
    hero = input("Hero name (make one up): ")
    key_answer = input("Do you have the golden key? (yes/no) ")
    has_key = key_answer.lower() == "yes"
    level = int(input("What level are you? "))
    if door_opens(has_key, level):
        # TODO 2: use an f-string so the message says the hero's name.
        print("The dragon door creaks open. Welcome!")
    else:
        print("The door stays shut. Find the key or reach level 10.")
Download starter.py

Stuck? Open a hint

Try on your own first. Hints open one at a time, from a small nudge to a bigger one. None of them gives the answer away.

Hint 1: Where to look

Read the three rules for the door at the top of the starter file. Right now door_opens() only checks the key. Does it ever look at the level?

Hint 2: Try this

Join two true-or-false checks with and when both must be true. Join them with or when either one is enough. Brackets ( ) keep a pair of checks together. For the message, an f-string puts a variable inside curly braces.

Hint 3: Almost there

The if line has this shape: if (____ and ____) or ____:. Match each blank to one of the rules. For the welcome, start the text with f and put the hero name inside braces, like print(f"... {____} ...").
